title: Self-Attention & Multiple Heads — Several Readers, Different Highlighters
key_insight: Self-attention lets positions in a sequence consult that same sequence. Multiple heads repeat the process with different learned projections.
body:
## Several Readers, Different Highlighters

One reader follows who “she” refers to; another notices dates; another tracks the main topic. One highlighting pattern cannot capture every relationship.

Self-attention lets positions in a sequence consult that same sequence. Multiple heads repeat the process with different learned projections.

The head results are joined and mixed. Heads are not assigned human labels in advance; useful roles emerge from training.
common_mistakes: Every attention head is manually programmed with a grammar rule.
Self-attention compares a sequence only with an unrelated database.
Causal language models should train by looking at future answers.
mini_exercise: Draw “Several Readers, Different Highlighters” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: This is the working mechanism that turns attention intuition into transformer representations.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Several Readers, Different Highlighters,” explain Self-Attention & Multiple Heads without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
